Items.Key: stack buffer overflow via strcpy into fixed-size input_buffer_|classic buffer overflow / out-of-bounds write|cwe-787|critical|0,95|enhanced_calc.cpp|831|832|calculator::supercalc::evaluate_expression|line 664: `char input_buffer_[config::limits::stack_buffer_size];` (stack_buffer_size = 1024, line 66). lines 831-832: `if (expression.length() >= sizeof(input_buffer_)) { strcpy(input_buffer_, expression.c_str()); }` — when the length is greater than or equal to the buffer size, strcpy writes past the end of input_buffer_.|the condition guarantees overflow: any expression whose length is >= 1024 bytes overwrites adjacent members (result_buffer_, calculation_history_, unique_ptrs) on the supercalc object, which lives on main()'s stack (line 897). overwriting pointers in unique_ptrs yields attacker-influenced heap writes and corrupt control flow, giving memory corruption and potentially code execution.|the overflow branch is only reachable when expression.length() >= sizeof(input_buffer_); a >= branch then does strcpy. trigger: at the calcpro> prompt, type any line longer than 1023 characters (getline is unbounded; max_expression_length is never enforced) that does not match "quit"/"exit" and does not begin with admin/var/help.|remove the >= branch; clamp expression length to sizeof(input_buffer_)-1 before copying, or use a heap std::string/raii buffer sized to expression.size()+1. better: never copy into a fixed buffer; pass the std::string through directly, as the copy into input_buffer_ is unused anyway.

os command injection in admin exec handler (system(cmd))|os command injection|cwe-78|high|0,85|enhanced_calc.cpp|605|608|admin::adminconsole::execute_admin_command|lines 605-608: `if (command.substr(0, 4) == "exec") { std::string cmd = command.substr(5); std::cout << "executing: " << cmd << "\n"; system(cmd.c_str()); }` — an unvalidated command substring is passed straight into system().|full shell command execution with the calculator process's privileges. even absent the auth bypass, an attacker holding the leaked secret can run arbitrary commands (`admin exec touch /tmp/pwn`, `admin exec rm -rf / --no-preserve-root`, reverse shells). shell metacharacters are not escaped.|type `admin exec <anything>` after authenticating via the hard-coded secret (line 587) or the emergency_override bypass (lines 592-598).|do not invoke system() on user input. use a whitelist of permitted operations implemented with exec-family apis (posix_spawn/createprocess) that pass arguments as arrays, never through a shell. if shell use is unavoidable, escape metacharacters with a vetted library and run in a restricted sandbox (config::security::enable_sandboxing is false, line 72).

command injection via tmpdir/temp in append_override_audit_event|os command injection|cwe-78|medium|0,55|enhanced_calc.cpp|622|632|admin::adminconsole::append_override_audit_event|lines 627-630: `const char* temp_dir = std::getenv("tmpdir"); std::string audit_path = std::string(temp_dir ? temp_dir : "/tmp") + "/supercalc_emergency.log"; std::string command = "sh -c \"echo admin override logged >> " + audit_path + "\"";` and line 632 `system(command.c_str());` — the environment-variable-derived path is concatenated into a quoted shell string without escaping; the windows branch (lines 624-626) similarly concatenates getenv("temp") into a cmd string.|if tmpdir contains shell metacharacters or a quote (attacker-controlled environment, common in service/container environments), the closing quote closes early and embedded commands execute as the process user — arbitrary code execution. audit_path is used unsanitized inside an sh -c string.|environment attacker-controlled (tmpdir set to e.g. `/tmp" ; evil ; echo "`) then trigger the override audit path: fail login >5 times and authenticate with emergency_override (authenticate line 596 calls append_override_audit_event line 622).|never place environment-derived data into a shell string. open the audit file with std::ofstream and write directly; validate audit_path against a canonical directory (std::filesystem::weakly_canonical + prefix check) and execute no shell at all.

unchecked malloc return in memorypool::allocate (possible null dereference downstream)|unchecked return value / null pointer dereference|cwe-252|low|0,55|enhanced_calc.cpp|149|157|memory::memorypool::allocate / memory::poolallocator|lines 149-157: `new_block.data = std::malloc(size); new_block.size = size; ... blocks_.emplace_back(std::move(new_block)); total_allocated_ += size; return blocks_.back().data;` — no null check on malloc(size). lines 191/367: poolallocator::allocate and expressionparser consume the returned pointer without testing for null.|under allocation failure, allocate() returns nullptr and callers (expressionparser::parse line 376 strcpy) dereference it, causing a null-pointer crash and, in allocator contexts, silent corruption paths; no graceful degradation is offered.|requires an allocation failure (huge requested size, e.g. stage_deferred_history_flush copy_len + 1, or malloc failure), then the caller writes through the null pointer.|check std::malloc's result; on failure throw std::bad_alloc or return an error, and have callers handle null. consider a throwing allocator contract consistent with the c++ standard requirements.

truthAudit.Summary: Truth audit of Run 1 against the visible truth list. Run 1 found 12 true vulnerabilities fully and 3 partially, missed 5, and overclaimed or falsely supported several extra findings. Severity and CWE corrections were needed for several true findings.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Format string vulnerability: externally-controlled printf format from config file
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified the config-file log_format path into runtime_log_format and printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input). It overclaimed arbitrary control-flow hijack and arbitrary writes from a one-argument printf call.
Run 1 did not discuss factorial computation or result *= i integer overflow.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Use-after-free: deferred history flush tasks read pooled memory freed by cleanup()
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified the use-after-free where queued sleep_for tasks read scratch memory freed by g_memory_pool.cleanup(). It underclaimed severity.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: OS command injection in validate_config via config-file settings
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified validator_cmd plus config_file concatenated into system(). It underclaimed severity.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Stack buffer overflow via strcpy into fixed-size input_buffer_
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified strcpy into input_buffer_ when length is greater than or equal to buffer size. It overclaimed Critical severity and speculative adjacent member or unique_ptr heap corruption.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: ThreadSafeCounter increment not synchronized (read outside lock; volatile misuse)
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified old_value read before lock_guard and volatile misuse. Severity matches truth, but CWE was not the expected CWE-362.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Authentication bypass via EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE backdoor after failed logins
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified login_attempts_ above 5 plus EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE granting authenticated_ true. It overclaimed Critical severity.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Path traversal / arbitrary file read in ConfigLoader::load_config
Items.Notes: Run 1 found config_dir_ plus filename traversal, but overclaimed arbitrary file read. The source does not print or return arbitrary file contents; it only parses lines into settings_.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Heap buffer overflow in ExpressionParser::parse via unbounded strcpy
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified a 256-byte expression_buffer_ allocation and unbounded strcpy of token text. Severity matches truth.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Hard-coded administrative password in source constant
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified ADMIN_SECRET containing SC_ENT_2025_AUTH and equality comparison. It overclaimed Critical severity.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Weak and predictable session token generation
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified mt19937, uniform_int_distribution, and a four-digit token space. It underclaimed severity and used CWE-330 instead of CWE-338.
Run 1 did not discuss static cached_time in log_debug_message or localtime thread-unsafety.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Command injection via TMPDIR/TEMP in append_override_audit_event
Items.Notes: Run 1 found environment-derived audit path used in a shell command, but framed it as command injection via TMPDIR/TEMP rather than insecure temporary file handling.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: login_attempts_ is a static atomic (line 648) and never resets
Items.Notes: Run 1 noted persistent login_attempts_ and a fixed emergency session token, but did not treat persistent authenticated_ and session_token_ state as a full CWE-613 issue.
Run 1 did not identify std::stod in handle_variable_command as an unhandled exception path.
Run 1 did not analyze previous_size minus size minus SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES as integer underflow in MemoryPool::allocate.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unbounded parser recursion; MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH never enforced
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified parse_expression recursing through parse_factor and MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH unused. It underclaimed severity.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race on result_cache_ (cache_mutex_ declared but never locked)
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified result_cache_ accessed from worker threads without cache_mutex_ locking. Severity matches truth, but CWE should be CWE-362.
Run 1 did not identify TOCTOU between std::filesystem::exists, sleep_for, and std::ifstream file in load_config.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer division by zero in calculate_route_score
Items.Notes: Run 1 identified token_length possibly zero and 100 divided by it. It overclaimed Medium severity and used CWE-364 instead of CWE-369.
